chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, who said: 'One of our companions informed me, raising it to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)'

He said: 'The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) was brought a man who was found in some ruins, and in his hand was a knife stained with blood, and behold, a slaughtered man was rolling in his blood. So the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) said to him: "What do you say?" He said: "O Commander of the Faithful! I killed him." He (peace be upon him) said: "Go with him and kill him." So when they went with him to kill him, a man came hurrying and said: "Do not be hasty, and return him to the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him)!" So they returned him.'

So he said: 'By Allah, O Commander of the Faithful! This one is not its perpetrator, it was I who killed him.' So the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) said to the first one: 'What carried you to confess against yourself when you did not do it?' He said: 'O Commander of the Faithful, and I did not have the ability to say (anything in my defense), and there had testified against me the likes of these men, and they seized me, and in my hand was a knife stained with blood, and the man was rolling in his blood, and I was standing over him, and I feared the beating, so I confessed.'

'And I am a man who had slaughtered a sheep by the side of these ruins, and the need for urination seized me, so I entered the ruins and saw the man rolling in his blood. So I stood there wondering, and these men came to me and seized me.'

So the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) said: 'Take these two and go with them both to Al-Hasan, and relate both their stories to him and say to him: "What is the ruling with regards to these two?"' So they went to Al-Hasan (peace be upon him) and related both their stories to him.

So Al-Hasan (peace be upon him) said: 'Say to the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him): "If this one has killed him, then he has revived this one, and Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: And whoever keeps it alive, it is as though he kept alive all men." Free them both and take the wergild of the slaughtered one from the public treasury."'
ai.seo_question: How did Imam Ali and Imam al-Hasan resolve a case of false confession and actual guilt in Islamic jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This narrative from Al-Kafi illustrates the principle of 'Al-Haqq al-Akhar' (the other right) in Shia jurisprudence, where Imam Ali (peace be upon him) referred the case to Imam al-Hasan (peace be upon him) to determine the status of the actual killer found at the scene. Imam al-Hasan ruled that since the false confessor was merely a witness to the crime and not the perpetrator, the actual killer should be released, and the victim's blood money (diyah) would be paid from the public treasury (bayt al-mal). This ruling highlights the distinction between personal rights and public rights in cases of homicide, emphasizing that the presence of the killer at the scene does not automatically negate the validity of the false confession for other purposes.
